text:
kai: heads-up — noticed a flurry of small-tenant evictions in the last hour, looks correlated with noisy short-lived prefixes :thinking_face:
rohan: seen that. spikes when many ephemeral requests touch a new prefix and get scored high immediately
emma: is this the usual eviction score decay issue or something else?
maria: fwiw our telemetry shows ~60% of those prefixes are 1-2 requests then never again, so aggressive eviction backfires and creates thrash
kai: my proposal: add a short debounce window and minimal sample threshold before treating a prefix as cold-evict candidate. basically require N samples or X seconds of inactivity after peak before hard-evict
rohan: makes sense. can be parametric per-tenant — small tenants should have lower thresholds so they don't hog space but also not get flapped out constantly
ash: tradeoff: longer debounce = higher memory usage under pathological workloads. We'll need a safety cap and a low-priority eviction lane to reclaim if global pressure hits a threshold
emma: can you sketch the config?
kai: sketch below:
```
{
  "eviction": {
    "debounce_ms": 5000,
    "min_hits": 3,
    "soft_evict_threshold": 0.75,
    "hard_reclaim_threshold": 0.95,
    "tenant_overrides": {
      "small": { "min_hits": 2, "debounce_ms": 2000 },
      "large": { "min_hits": 5, "debounce_ms": 10000 }
    }
  }
}
```
rohan: nice. also add an "inflight_protection" bit — if a prefix has in-flight requests, don't evict until inflight drops to 0 or timeout. avoids mid-request eviction races
maria: for correctness, we should ensure prefix handoff / ownership checks continue to hold if debounce delays logical demotion. basically lease must still be valid to avoid dual ownership
kai: agreed. plan: debounce only affects the eviction decision; it does not change lease transfer semantics. we keep leases authoritative, debounce sits in admission/score stage
ash: what about metrics? We should produce an "eviction_debounce_count" per tenant class and add a gauge for "debounce_memory_overhead" estimated
emma: and a regression test: simulate 10k ephemeral prefixes with Poisson arrivals and verify tail latency doesn't increase and eviction counts drop
rohan: small implementation note: keep debounce state compact (ring buffer of recent touch timestamps + hit counter) so we don't bloat the cache meta
maria: concur. also add a canary rollout: enable debounce for 5% hosts, monitor eviction_rate, thrash_rate, memory_pressure for 60m
ash: edge-case: what if tenant intentionally uses many prefixes as a pattern (e.g., per-user routing)? debounce could hide real hotset growth. we need a heuristic to escalate if growth is sustained (exponentially-backoff threshold reduction)
kai: good call. propose: sliding-window growth detector that reduces min_hits if prefix demonstrates increasing hit-rate trend
rohan: implementable. I'll spike this afternoon and post a PR with config flags + metrics.
ops-bot: deploy-canary: started rollout of eviction-debounce v1 to 5% cluster on zone-a at 2026-03-20T15:34:00Z :rocket:
emma: thanks — after PR link we should sync with SRE to pick canary hosts and alert thresholds
ash: ok i'll set up alerts for eviction_debounce_count > baseline*5 and memory_overhead_gauge > 2% above normal
kai: thanks all. follow-ups: PR by rohan, simple simulation by emma, canary watch by ash/maria.
